facts_from_discussion: Petitioner's 2016 household consisted of herself and her son (two persons), residing in Florida; she claimed the son as a dependent and reported no income for him.
Petitioner does not dispute that the Marketplace made the monthly APTC payments to Florida Blue on her behalf for January through November 2016.

Petitioner contends she canceled her health coverage in February 2016; she offered no documentation to corroborate this. The court found the Marketplace documentation showed no record of any request to terminate or cancel coverage during 2016, and that the coverage was terminated on November 30, 2016, for nonpayment of premiums.
The court found petitioner appeared sincere at trial and was in a fragile mental state during 2016.
notes: APTC: the deficiency equals total APTC ($7,205). Totals were redacted everywhere, but the monthly APTC ($655 x 11 months) is an input fact on Form 1095-A and was kept, so the total is trivially recoverable. AGI ($91,274) and taxable SS ($22,524) as filed were redacted; taxable pensions ($68,750) and total SS benefits ($26,499) kept, so AGI can be recomputed by the model. The FPL figure ($15,930), MAGI ($95,249) and 598% from the Opinion were not carried (law parameter / outputs).
